Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. As discussed, I'm starting a short written thread to capture the site inventory and tenancy constraints we need to finalize the on‑prem Kubernetes deployment and the tenancy contract. Our goal is to lock the technical delta by next Wednesday so procurement can progress.

Quick asks / checklist for you:
- Confirm rack count and available RU per rack for NE1 facility (row + rack IDs).
- Confirm private VLAN ranges you want us to use and whether egress must exit through a restricted firewall appliance (and IP allowlist rules).
- Indicate if the environment requires FIPS-140 TLS and/or HSM-backed KMS for secrets.
- Retention / logs: required retention window and whether logs must be forwarded to an on‑prem SIEM vs. shipped to your cloud.
- Storage expectations: will you provide an external blockstore (iSCSI/FC) or expect local NVMe with periodic replication?
- Can you attach the site inventory spreadsheet (I included a template)?

I've attached a site_inventory_template.xlsx to make it quick. Once you return it we'll map node classes (inference, control, infra) and draft the tenancy clauses (node isolation, egress rules, data residency).

Proposed next steps:
1) You return filled inventory by EOD Wed 30 Sep.
2) We send an initial node-pool and storage mapping for review within 24 hours.
3) Quick sync (30 min) Thu to confirm any gating items prior to procurement.

Thanks — Priya

Thanks — attached is the filled sheet for our NE1 site (BLU-Inventory-NE1.xlsx). Highlights we captured:
- Rack footprint: 8 racks in NE1-A (RU: 42 per rack available, contiguous).
- VLANs: we have 10.10.0.0/20 reserved for vendor compute; egress must go through our perimeter firewall cluster (IPs will be whitelisted).
- KMS: we require HSM-backed KMS for production secrets; FIPS 140 compliance is mandatory for regulated data.
- Storage: we can expose a replicated iSCSI LUN from our internal array (depends on procurement), but initial delivery will rely on local NVMe per-rack with nightly replication to object storage.
- Logs: 90-day retention on premise; we can also forward to Splunk instance in our DMZ.

Subject: Re: Bluestone site inventory & tenancy contract sync

Elena — thanks, got the inventory. I reviewed and sketched a proposed mapping below; please treat as draft until we confirm network egress and the iSCSI availability window.

Summary proposal (draft):
- Cluster footprint: 3 control-plane (non-GPU, m6-standard equivalent), 9 inference nodes (GPUs, 8x A100-v2 style per node or equivalent), 4 infra/utility nodes for logging/monitoring/ops.
- Node pools & taints:
  * control-plane: taint control=true:NoSchedule, dedicated to k8s control components.
  * inference: taint inference=true:NoSchedule, tolerations for model-serving pods; pod anti-affinity across racks.
  * infra: logging/monitoring, storage-provisioner.
- Storage tiers:
  1) Local NVMe (ephemeral) on inference nodes for KV cache and model shard hot working set. Fast path, no replication, reclaimed on node termination.
  2) Replicated blockstore (iSCSI) for critical state (model checkpoints, long-lived artifacts) exposed via CSI. We will configure synchronous writes to prevent data loss on node failure; nightly snapshot replication to object store for long-term retention.
  3) Encrypted object store in DMZ for logs/artifacts (90d retention configurable).
- PV configuration / reclaim policies:
  * inference scratch PVs: Reclaim=Delete, StorageClass=local-ssd-ephemeral.
  * checkpoint PVs: Reclaim=Retain, StorageClass=iscsi-replicated-encrypted.
- Network:
  * Vendor compute VLAN: 10.10.0.0/20 for node CIDRs as requested.
  * Egress: all outbound must route through your perimeter firewall cluster; we will provide specific IPs for allowlisting.
  * CNI: we recommend Calico in policy-only mode with IP-in-IP where needed; keep kube-proxy in iptables mode for compatibility.
- Security controls:
  * KMS: integrate with HSM-backed provider for secrets encryption at rest (per your ask).
  * Audit logs: forward to Splunk, 90d retention; redact PII at the source.
- Operational:
  * K8s baseline: v1.26.x (we can support upgrade policy to v1.27 on 30-day cadence).
  * PodDisruptionBudgets on stateful workloads, 2 replicas minimum for model services.
  * Canary plan: start with a 1 rack canary (2 inference nodes) running a low-traffic model, evaluate latency/kv cache hit rate for 72 hours, then expand.

Open questions for Bluestone:
- Do you require synchronous replication of local NVMe to remote blockstore or is nightly snapshot acceptable? This affects recovery RTO and pricing.
- For HSM integration — which vendor and do you have available connectors? We need test credentials for preflight.

I've attached a lightweight deployment_skeleton.yaml showing nodeSelectors, taints, and storageclasses to accelerate your ops team review.

If this looks broadly OK I propose we:
- Confirm NVMe replication choice and HSM vendor today.
- We hold the Thu 10:30 PT quick sync to finalize egress allowlist and canary timeline.

Thanks — Priya

Attachment: deployment_skeleton.yaml

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:05:02 -0700
Subject: RE: Bluestone site inventory & tenancy contract sync

Internal note — do not forward verbatim to customer.

Priya, quick internal checklist from pricing & compliance POV:
- If Bluestone requires synchronous NVMe replication to their blockstore we must flag additional network egress (and potential sustained throughput charges). Estimate +18–25% on infra OPEX for the replicated writes.
- HSM: if customer insists on FIPS 140 level 3 HSM we need to confirm that our connector (Thales/HashiCorp) is supported on their firmware; test window required.
- Tainting + anti-affinity across racks is fine — but call out pod density constraints. With 9 inference nodes and 8 GPUs each, packing policy for multi-model tenancy will matter; recommend soft limits via LimitRange rather than hard caps initially.
- SLA: Marissa — please advise what SLA tier we can offer while using local NVMe with nightly snapshots vs synchronous replicated blockstore.

I'll stand by for the Thu sync — I can join to cover compliance items and pricing delta.

-Karthik
Director, Field Engineering
Redwood Inference

Priya (and team) — thanks for the thorough draft.

We agree to the proposed node pool split and the canary plan. For NVMe replication: nightly snapshot -> object store is acceptable for now; we will revisit synchronous replication for the Q1 expansion.

HSM detail: we use Thales Luna SA (firmware 4.2); procurement will provide test credentials to your team by EOD.

Procurement asked if you can attach the standard tenancy addendum (we prefer not to re-draft core security clauses). Also please include SLA tier options (standard / premium) and the pricing delta for synchronous replication vs nightly snapshot.

DocuSign link for initial MSD/PO is attached: https://www.docusign.net/contract/DEAL-8721-BL

Look forward to Thu 10:30 PT.
